question: Under the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) programme, which population receives the weekly IFA supplement?

answers.text: Pregnant women in the first trimester only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pregnant women receive daily IFA supplementation (180 tablets throughout pregnancy), not the weekly WIFS dose. WIFS targets a different group.

answers.text: School-going adolescent girls and boys aged 10–19 years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. WIFS targets adolescents aged 10–19 years — both girls and boys in government schools — with a weekly supervised dose of IFA (large blue tablet: 100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) to reduce iron-deficiency anaemia.
Children 6–59 months receive iron supplementation under the IYCF/NHM child health programme (weekly IFA syrup), but they are not the WIFS programme target group.
Non-pregnant WRA can receive IFA under National Iron Plus Initiative, but the WIFS programme specifically targets adolescents (10–19 years) in schools.

overallFeedback.feedback: WIFS (Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation) targets adolescent girls and boys aged 10–19 years in government schools. The dose is one large blue IFA tablet (100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) per week under supervision.
Correct. WIFS targets adolescents 10–19 years in government and aided schools with a weekly supervised IFA dose (100 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid).
